To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a direct transition from vesicular structures to cubosomes is possible in monoelaidin aqueous dispersion in presence of the polyoxyethylenated block copolymer F127.
the temperature-induced structural transition in the ME dispersion in the presence F127 is different from that of its bulk system.
the direct transition of monoelaidineous vesicle dispersion to cubosome phase is possible.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the formation and structural characterization of ME dispersion, and it may provide a better understanding of the structure-property relationship of this novel dispersion system.
the formation of highly swollen cubosomes and hexosomes in aqueous dispersions of ME, which can be used as potential carriers for drug delivery.
the self-assembly in ME aqueous dispersions and its potential for the design of novel cubosomes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of the stabilizer leads to the formation and stabilization of a swollen Im3m cubic phase in the dispersion.
F127 has a stabilizing effect on the cubosomes and the formed particles are less sensitive to temperature fluctuations.
the presence of a polymeric stabilizer in the system has a significant influence on the formation of the nanostructures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the polymeric F127 is a powerful tool in the preparation of highly swollen nanostructured dispersions.
the polymeric surfactant F127 can be used to stabilize the internal nanostructure of cubosomes.
the formation of cubosomes and hexosomes in the ME dispersion is possible by heating the dispersion.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the formation of cubosomes and hexosomes is not restricted to MO and that the formation of these structures in aqueous dispersions is a generic phenomenon, which is not necessarily related to the chemical structure and phase behavior of the lipids.

the formation of cubosomes in aqueous dispersion of ME is not only possible but also that the transition from lamellar to nonlamellar phase occurs at lower temperature as compared to the fully hydrated bulk system.

the dispersion system is not only a good candidate for the study of the structural transitions of lipids, but also a promising system for the development of novel nanostructured lipid-based delivery vehicles.
